Life insurance for Louisiana residents

Life insurance pays a sum to the people you name when you die. The right kind depends on what the money has to do: pay for a funeral, replace a paycheck while children are at home, clear a mortgage, or last your whole life. Louisiana has 4,573,749 residents. 793,655 of them are 65 or older (17.4%), and another 291,290 are between 60 and 64, according to Census Bureau 2023 population estimates. We ask what you need the coverage to do, compare what several insurers offer for your age and health, and explain the differences in plain English.

Insurers pay us a commission when a policy is placed. The insurer, not the agent, decides whether you are approved and what you pay.

Types of life insurance we help with in Louisiana

Final expense and burial insurance

Final expense insurance, also called burial insurance, is a smaller whole life policy meant to pay for a funeral and last bills. The premium stays level and the coverage does not end while premiums are paid. Many policies ask health questions instead of requiring a medical exam. Some accept every applicant in an age range and pay a reduced benefit if death from illness happens in the first years, so it matters which kind you are offered. How final expense insurance works.

Term life

Term life covers a set number of years. If you die during the term, the insurer pays the benefit to the people you name. If you outlive the term, the coverage ends. It is often chosen while a household depends on a paycheck. How term life works.

Mortgage protection

Mortgage protection is life insurance sized to a home loan. It is usually a term policy that you own, with the benefit paid to the person you name, not to the lender. It is different from the mortgage insurance a lender may require. How mortgage protection works.

Whole life

Whole life is permanent coverage with a level premium and a cash value that grows on a schedule written into the policy. It costs more than term for the same benefit. How whole life works.

Indexed universal life (IUL)

Indexed universal life is permanent coverage with a cash value account. Interest is credited by the movement of a market index, within a cap and a floor set by the insurer. You are not invested in the index, policy charges can change, and loans reduce the death benefit. It is life insurance first, not an investment. How IUL works, and who it fits.

Coverage on a child or grandchild

A small whole life policy on a child can suit some families once the parents are covered. When it fits and when it does not.

How a review works when you live in Louisiana

  1. Schedule a life insurance review on PlanEnroll and choose Life as the meeting type. You can also call or text us.
  2. We ask what the coverage needs to do, about your health and tobacco use, and what premium is comfortable.
  3. We compare policies from the insurers we are appointed with in Louisiana and explain how they differ.
  4. If you apply, the insurer reviews the application. Depending on the policy it may ask health questions, check records or ask for an exam.
  5. When the policy is issued we go through it with you, and we are here when something in your life changes.

Louisiana facts to check before you buy

  • Free look period. The Louisiana Department of Insurance guide says Louisiana law allows you a 10-day free look period to decide whether to keep a life insurance policy.
  • Prepaid funeral contracts. La. R.S. 37:865 limits how a funeral establishment may use money paid on a preneed funeral contract, requires those payments to go into trust accounts or to an insurer, and requires an annual sworn report of the accounts to the Louisiana State Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors, which can inspect the records.
  • Consumer guide. The Louisiana Department of Insurance publishes a Consumer’s Guide to Life Insurance (Rev. 12/2025).

Sources for this section, read November 27, 2026: Louisiana Department of Insurance, Consumer’s Guide to Life Insurance (Rev. 12/2025); Louisiana Revised Statutes 37:865. Rules can change; the policy or contract you are given states its own terms.

Who regulates life insurance in Louisiana

The Louisiana Department of Insurance regulates insurers and agents in Louisiana. It can verify an agent’s license and answer consumer questions. Licensed agent Luay Sadqi (NPN 21370662) holds a license for Louisiana.

Common questions

Life insurance in Louisiana: questions

Do I need to visit an office to buy life insurance in Louisiana?
No. Our office is in Tysons, Virginia, and we help Louisiana residents by phone or video call. Office visits are by appointment in Northern Virginia only.
Is Honorbrook licensed in Louisiana?
Yes. Licensed agent Luay Sadqi (NPN 21370662) holds a license for Louisiana. You can verify any agent’s license with the Louisiana Department of Insurance.
Will I need a medical exam?
It depends on the policy. Many final expense policies ask health questions instead of requiring an exam. Larger term and permanent policies often involve a health interview, a records check or an exam. The insurer decides what it needs.
What does a life insurance review cost?
Nothing. You do not pay us a fee. Insurers pay us a commission when a policy is placed.
Which meeting type do I choose when I schedule?
Choose Life. PlanEnroll offers Life, Health and Annuities. Medicare is a Health meeting, and retirement income is an Annuities meeting.
